text:
Calgary arrives on a four-game winning streak after beating Toronto 5-2 on Monday, but we're not sure it's as strong as it looks. The Flames have had 47% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five, and their goalies have saved 6.8 goals more than expected during the run. They're without Samuel Honzek. Edmonton is in game five of a five-game home stand, coming off a 4-3 shootout loss to Detroit, and plays without Mattias Ekholm (upper body) and Jason Dickinson. With Ekholm out, Evan Bouchard has gone up to 28:56 a night from 25:48.

The Oilers have the better chance profile (2.99 expected goals for per 60 minutes against 2.73 allowed, versus 2.94 and 3.30 for Calgary), and our model projects 3.06 goals for Edmonton and 2.77 for Calgary. Edmonton's power play generates 0.93 expected goals a game to Calgary's 0.47, and Calgary takes 4.6 penalties a game. The goalie matchup is the question: projected starter Tristan Jarry is 6.5 goals worse than expected this season, while Calgary's projected Devin Cooley is 2.4 better.

Connor McDavid has a 12-game point streak and a 93% chance of a point, and Leon Draisaitl has a 46% chance to score. For Calgary, Joel Farabee has points in five straight and a 27% chance to score. As Hockey Patrol reported, the league has ruled on Draisaitl's cross-check on Auston Matthews.
